headline: President, PM send Durga Puja greetings to all citizens
summary: The heads of state and government emphasized creating a safe environment for all citizens to practice their religious rituals during the festival.
details: President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman issued messages of harmony as the formalities of Durga Puja, the biggest religious festival for Bangladeshi Hindus, began.

Both leaders emphasized the importance of creating a safe environment for all citizens to practice their respective religious rituals and ceremonies, reiterating their commitment to ensuring such security.
The President noted that Durga Puja embodies a call for justice and humanity, symbolizing the triumph of truth, beauty, and welfare over evil forces.
He highlighted that the Hindu community has long celebrated the festival in a festive atmosphere, reflecting the enduring communal harmony and social culture of Bengal.
The President also mentioned government support for the renovation of religious institutions and the provision of monthly honorariums to priests.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman stated that equality, human dignity, and social justice are fundamental to all religions, with the welfare of humanity being a principal teaching.
Referring to the recent political changeover, the Prime Minister noted that Bangladesh is resuming its democratic journey and is committed to establishing a safe and humane nation for all citizens.
He urged all members of the Hindu community to celebrate Durga Puja peacefully and safely, stating that while everyone has their own religion, the state belongs to all.
caption:
President and PM issue messages of harmony for Durga Puja, pledging a safe environment for all citizens to celebrate.

President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman issued messages of harmony as the formalities of Durga Puja, the biggest religious festival for Bangladeshi Hindus, began.

Both leaders emphasized the importance of creating a safe environment for all citizens to practice their respective religious rituals and ceremonies, reiterating their commitment to ensuring such security.

The President noted that Durga Puja embodies a call for justice and humanity, symbolizing the triumph of truth, beauty, and welfare over evil forces.

He highlighted that the Hindu community has long celebrated the festival in a festive atmosphere, reflecting the enduring communal harmony and social culture of Bengal.

The President also mentioned government support for the renovation of religious institutions and the provision of monthly honorariums to priests.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman stated that equality, human dignity, and social justice are fundamental to all religions, with the welfare of humanity being a principal teaching.

Referring to the recent political changeover, the Prime Minister noted that Bangladesh is resuming its democratic journey and is committed to establishing a safe and humane nation for all citizens.

He urged all members of the Hindu community to celebrate Durga Puja peacefully and safely, stating that while everyone has their own religion, the state belongs to all.

headline: Man shot to death in Rajbari by motorcycle-borne attackers
summary: The victim, Piarul Sardar, was shot twice by two men on a motorcycle; police say he was accused in 13 to 14 criminal cases.
details: A 32-year-old man named Piarul Sardar was shot dead on Friday evening at Sajnokanda in Rajbari’s Sadar upazila.
According to Rajbari SP Mir Monir Hossain, Piarul was standing about 200 metres from his home around 6:45 pm when two men on a motorcycle fired two shots at him.
Locals rushed to the spot and took him to Rajbari Sadar Hospital, then referred to Faridpur Medical College Hospital, but he died on the way.
The body is currently at the Rajbari Sadar Hospital morgue.
District police are currently reviewing CCTV footage to identify the perpetrators and several teams are working on the case.
SP Monir also noted that the victim, Piarul Sardar, was an accused in 13 to 14 cases involving drugs, arms, and murder.
caption:
A man was shot dead by motorcycle-borne attackers in Rajbari. Police say the victim was accused in over a dozen criminal cases.

A 32-year-old man named Piarul Sardar was shot dead on Friday evening at Sajnokanda in Rajbari’s Sadar upazila.

According to Rajbari SP Mir Monir Hossain, Piarul was standing about 200 metres from his home around 6:45 pm when two men on a motorcycle fired two shots at him.

Locals rushed to the spot and took him to Rajbari Sadar Hospital, then referred to Faridpur Medical College Hospital, but he died on the way.

The body is currently at the Rajbari Sadar Hospital morgue.

District police are currently reviewing CCTV footage to identify the perpetrators and several teams are working on the case.

SP Monir also noted that the victim, Piarul Sardar, was an accused in 13 to 14 cases involving drugs, arms, and murder.
